purpose: Test whether a wider separation between source pulses separates source order from unknown cue strength using unchanged post-cue observations.
scientific_risk_addressed: Observation-time selection improved fitted calibration separation but left the fresh cohort at 29/32, trading one gain for one regression. Avoid tuning readers or lowering the margin on inspected cases; test one controlled physical input change using calibration cases only.

design.source_order: Unchanged: source 1 first/source 4 second, or the reverse.
design.dose: Same integrated inhibition per source, cue strength and location; 75/25 versus 25/75 shares and equal 50/50 order-only control. No increase in dose or pulse width.
design.reader: Same nearest-calibrated-polyline reader; independent calibration for each physical protocol, no rescaling or feature search.
design.baseline: Reuse authenticated baseline calibration trajectories; do not resimulate or score the inspected held-out cohort.
design.selection_inputs: Only the three calibration strengths. Load and rank no held-out response arrays, targets or resolution counts.
design.objective: Reuse half the minimum distance between opposite-label fitted curves, including segment interiors and endpoints; take the minimum across joint tasks, relevant single-task controls and all three timesteps. Null controls are reported separately.
design.decision: Report both protocols. Prefer the baseline for ties within 1e-15 V or any backend winner disagreement; consider the candidate for fresh confirmation only for reproducible improvement. Report separately whether the fitted-curve minimum exceeds 2 nV and by how much.
design.no_guarantee: A fitted-curve improvement, including one above 2 nV, is not a bound on continuous physical responses or biological noise. The earlier 29/32 result remains unchanged.

verification: Authenticate the completed baseline and unchanged production physics before the new run.
Check exact physical event indices and per-source integrated doses at all three timesteps; all primary observation times must follow cue removal.
Compare unchanged no-cue and location-only calibration histories bitwise, and the common pre-104-us prefix for other arms, using saved baseline identities.
Retain full state archives, conservation/domain checks, CPU/L4 tolerances, reordered/partitioned worlds and restart across the changed second pulse.
Retain independent curve-geometry and calibration-isolation tests; fixed coarse/fine criteria and controls cannot be relaxed for improved resolution.
Report both GPU-busy and measured SM-active with coverage, actual per-arm kernel/archive timing and equal world-step budgets.

followup.decision: If justified by calibration geometry, freeze the chosen pulse protocol before a separate confirmation on new strengths, including weak cues near 0.4. Do not reuse the diagnosed cohort as fresh evidence.

execution: Reuse the existing bounded windowed runner. Expected runs of at least 10 minutes must be detached with durable result/failure artifacts, without automatic polling or follow-up.
scope: Synthetic input-encoding experiment using the verified bioelectric layer. No new native BETSE parity or biological calibration claim.
